I've finished the review. I made no changes and recorded no approval.

## What I inspected myself
- **Actual job:** all six frames listed in `final-render.json` for job f384 r0 (checkpoint `1f3568cb…`): front three-quarter, rear three-quarter, front, left, right and top.
- **Approved source job:** the 2ee3 r2 contact sheet. I also opened two source frames at full 1000 px from the same run (front three-quarter and front) for a side-by-side check.
- **Records:**
  - Read in full: `final-validation.json`, `final-actual-correspondence-reviewer-v1.json`, `retained-registry-independent-audit-v1.json`, `independent-selected-partition-index-v2.json` and `final-native-receipts.json`.
  - Read only the first lines: `final-status.json`, `final-dimensions.json` and `final-export.json`.

## Visual findings (from the images)
- **Silhouette:** no change I can see in any of the six views. Gun length and elevation, both antennas, the bustle rack, the commander's and loader's weapon stations, the smoke grenade launchers, the side-skirt outline, 7 road wheels per side, the sprocket, the idler and the track run all match the source sheet.
- **Full-resolution pairs:** the two pairs I opened look the same, down to small details like the light edge lines on the turret and the three lower-glacis colour bands.
- **Seams and holes:** none added. The new splits (skirts, blow-off panels, rear exhaust grilles, edge highlights and seam accents) show no gaps, slivers, z-fighting or missing faces.
- **Exhaust grille:** it still reads as three bays in the rear three-quarter view and as continuous bars in the top view, consistent with `engineGrilleWhole: true`.
- **Assembly and shading:** no parts are displaced, doubled or floating, and no faces look flipped or wrongly shaded. The flat-shaded faceting matches the source.
- **Already in the source, not caused by the split:**
  - a thin white gap between the hull and the fenders in the front view
  - a small dark sliver at the lower front of the hull in the left view
  - the bands of grilles on the turret roof and hull deck in the top view
- **Two limits on these visual checks:**
  - They are by eye only; I didn't diff pixels. In the final render file, the actual front three-quarter frame has the same `pixelHash` as its own baseline render pass, so re-rendering is stable. I didn't see the source frames' pixel hashes, so I can't confirm pixel-identical output.
  - I didn't open the other four source frames at full resolution, only at the contact sheet's reduced size.

## Records (what they say; I didn't re-run any of these checks)
- **Validation:** passed, deterministic, no issues. 38,184 triangles, 10 materials, 0 textures, 340 objects.
- **Correspondence (source vs actual):**
  - 260 meshes kept exactly from the source, plus 19 new meshes that map exactly back to source faces, for 279 in total.
  - Triangle, normal and material multisets are exact, and source mesh world and local matrices are exact.
  - The 19 new meshes have no UVs. The parenting under the original assembly roots is exact.
- **Registry audit:**
  - 51 parts; 260 meshes each owned by exactly one part, plus 9 reserved (the source meshes that were split).
  - Each track assembly (P69, P70) holds 96 meshes, so individual track shoes can be swapped.
  - Source materials are shared across parts: paint across 33 parts, rubber across 31, steel across 21.
- **Native isolation:** `final-native-receipts.json` names 4 receipts covering 279 components, with `allPass` and `statePreserved` true. I didn't open the receipts.
- **Dimensions:** I read only the opening section: 16 asset-level criteria (envelope, datums, origin, pivot, grounding) scoped to the rest pose. I didn't reach the per-component results, so the claim that all 279 pass comes from your brief, not from my reading.

## Partitioning for future damage replacements
- **Adequate for swapping parts.** The splits are where damage swaps are most likely: skirts, blow-off panels, exhaust grilles and per-shoe tracks. The hull and engine grille are kept whole, and the body has no new cuts.
- **Pivots:** every part wrapper sits at the world origin (identity matrix) under the original hull and turret assemblies. That works for swapping a part in place. It does not give per-part pivots for hinged or detaching damage.
- **Articulated ancestry:** the records say it's intact. That is static hierarchy evidence, not proof that the parts animate correctly.
- **Materials:** 70 parts hold separate selection owners but share source materials. Any per-part scorch or paint change will need cloned and re-bound materials; changing a shared material would recolour the whole tank.

## Unresolved gaps and blockers
1. **Root independent check still running.** The aggregate check of all 279 isolation results isn't finished, and I didn't verify the 4 receipt files themselves.
2. **Per-component dimensions not seen by me.** I didn't read past the start of the dimensions file.
3. **No pixel diff against the source.** There's no source-vs-actual pixel comparison bound to hashes, and 4 of the source views were only compared at reduced size.
4. **Material ownership** is not per part (see above). This blocks per-part material edits, not this clean source.
5. **Pivots** are at the world origin, so hinged or detaching damage can't be authored without new pivots.
6. **Exhaust bays and deck bars** are simplified model geometry; their counts haven't been checked against reference (the partition index says so itself).

## Recommendation
- **Source fidelity:** the actual r0 renders look the same as the approved desert M1A1 r2 source in all six views, and the records support the preservation claim.
- **Modular direction:** I recommend continuing with this partition as the clean modular base. Close gaps 1 and 2 first. Plan cloned materials and new pivots as the first steps of any damage work.

This is not approval, a score, a human decision or a runtime qualification.
